newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold, bears eye weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold, bears eye weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly held steady Tuesday in thin trade, but mild East Coast weather and flagging utility demand raised bearish expectations, market sources said.

"The weather doesn't look all that supportive - there's not much heat on the horizon - but, if the East Coast gets hot again, you'll see prices shoot right back up," said one cash trader, noting utility burns this week were sagging due to mild temperatures and competitive gas prices.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent held steady at about $16.25 a barrel, with August one percent paper done unchanged at $16.20. September paper sold at $16.05, flat from Monday's levels, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also was little changed at about $17.50.
High sulphurs in New York showed little movement, with 2.2 percent still talked at $15.00-25.
At the U.S. Gulf, three percent again was stable at $14.50-75, while one percent slipped another quarter to $15.25-50.

New York city gate swing gas prices held relatively steady Tuesday in the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.25 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained a couple of cents to $2.22/mmBtu, or $13.99 a barrel.
